series.premise: Fourteen-year-old Leela Joshi inherits a rain-soaked mansion where every door bears a name—except hers—and anyone who sleeps inside is forgotten by sunrise.
series.season_engine: Each room holds a person erased from family history; solving its emotional truth returns one relationship while revealing why Leela's grandmother helped the house consume names.
series.ending_promise: Leela must free the forgotten without turning their names into possessions or erasing the living people who replaced them.
series.global_image_style: Vertical 9:16 premium cute cinematic 3D feature-animation, original compact stylized characters with large expressive eyes, monsoon-gothic Indian mansion, carved dark wood, moss, rain-glass, warm oil lamps and restrained spectral cyan light, tactile fabric and architecture, emotionally truthful acting, eerie but never graphic; preserve all locked character sheets exactly.

characters.name: Leela Joshi
characters.lock: small Indian teen girl, warm brown skin, huge black-brown eyes, oval face, thick wavy black hair cut at shoulders with one white streak near right temple, moss-green raincoat over maroon kurta, navy leggings, brown lace boots, brass label-maker hanging from belt
characters.acting: skepticism through narrowed focus; tenderness appears before she admits belief

characters.name: Avi Joshi
characters.lock: tiny Indian boy, warm brown skin, round cheeks, large dark eyes, tousled black hair, sunflower-yellow hoodie, denim overalls, red rain boots, stuffed grey elephant with one button eye
characters.acting: fear and curiosity coexist; never reduced to comic relief

characters.name: Noor
characters.role: nameless ghost girl bound to the house
characters.lock: small translucent Indian girl about fifteen, luminous cyan-grey eyes, long floating black hair, faded indigo school dress from 1978, bare feet, blank brass nameplate pinned over heart
characters.acting: controlled stillness; expression flickers when memories return

characters.name: Devika Joshi
characters.role: Leela's grandmother and former Keeper of Names
characters.lock: elderly Indian woman, medium brown skin, alert dark eyes, silver hair in loose bun, rust-red sari beneath charcoal shawl, wooden walking stick containing hidden fountain pen, seven empty name tags around wrist
characters.acting: sharp practical love burdened by specific guilt

characters.name: Samir Dutt
characters.role: fifteen-year-old local history vlogger whose own sister was erased
characters.lock: lean Indian teen boy, deep brown skin, large hazel eyes, short curly black hair, cobalt windbreaker, beige cargo trousers, black sneakers, compact analog camcorder with green strap
characters.acting: talks fast when scared, lowers camera when truth matters more than proof

characters.name: Mr Harrow
characters.role: polite estate archivist who feeds unresolved names to the house
characters.lock: very tall thin Indian man late fifties, pale-brown skin, small silver eyes, slick black-grey hair, immaculate cream suit, dark gloves, long black umbrella, leather ledger chained to wrist
characters.acting: perfect courtesy without warmth; anger appears only as lost rhythm

characters.name: The House
characters.role: living archive built from forgotten relationships
characters.lock: monsoon-dark three-storey Indian hill mansion, asymmetric tiled roofs, moss-covered carved balconies, one round attic window glowing cyan, front door with hundreds of blank brass labels
characters.acting: emotion through doors, settling timber, lamp color and spatial impossibility; no literal face

episodes.title: The House Had No Name for Her
episodes.logline: Leela enters her inheritance and finds every family name on the door except hers.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leela enters the house and hears Noor ask for her stolen name.
episodes.location: front hall of the monsoon-dark mansion
beats: Leela arrives during a storm and finds hundreds of brass family labels covering the front door.
Avi finds his own label warm beneath his fingers, but Leela's name is absent.
Devika warns them to leave before sunset and refuses to explain the inheritance.
The door locks itself when Leela says her full name aloud.
Every portrait turns its painted face away from her.
A blank label appears over Leela's bedroom and begins engraving one letter by itself.
Leela rips it free before the last letter forms.
From inside the wall, Noor whispers: that was my name first.

episodes.title: Everyone Forgot Avi by Morning
episodes.logline: The house erases Avi from family memory after he sleeps beneath his label.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leela becomes the only person who remembers Avi and learns written anchors resist erasure.
episodes.location: Avi's shifting bedroom and breakfast room
beats: Leela wakes to find Avi's bedroom replaced by a linen cupboard.
Devika insists Leela arrived alone and has never had a brother.
Family photos show an empty space where Avi stood.
Leela's handwritten puzzle book still contains Avi's answers.
She follows muddy red-boot prints into a corridor too narrow for the house.
Avi sits behind wallpaper while his voice fades from Leela's memory.
Leela writes his name on her own arm and pulls him through.
The rescued Avi casts no reflection, proving the house kept part of him.

episodes.title: The Mirror Kept His Reflection
episodes.logline: Avi's reflection offers to return if Leela gives the house one different name.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leela refuses substitution and cracks open the first room archive.
episodes.location: long mirror gallery
beats: Avi's reflection smiles from a mirror after the real boy looks away.
It says the house balances every returned person with another forgotten name.
Leela considers offering Mr Harrow, the unknown executor named in the will.
Noor appears in the glass and asks whether a stranger is easier to erase.
Leela rejects the bargain and labels the mirror with the truth: Avi is missing, not replaced.
The glass cracks without breaking and releases Avi's reflection.
Behind it lies a classroom preserved from 1978.
Every desk bears a name except the one where Noor is sitting.

episodes.title: The Ghost Failed Her Own Name
episodes.logline: Noor cannot speak her identity because the house punishes guessed names.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Noor joins Leela under a chosen temporary name.
episodes.location: preserved 1978 classroom
beats: The classroom bell rings and Noor is forced to repeat an attendance ritual.
Every wrong name makes one of her memories disappear from the blackboard.
Avi calls her Noor because moonlight crosses her face, not because he claims it is true.
The house accepts a chosen nickname without consuming it.
Leela finds Devika's teenage signature on the old attendance sheet.
Noor remembers Devika locking the classroom during a fire alarm.
Leela promises to investigate without forcing Noor to forgive.
The classroom door opens into Devika's current bedroom, where she has been listening.

episodes.title: Grandmother Locked the Classroom
episodes.logline: Devika admits she saved the village by letting the house erase one classroom.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Devika confesses her role and gives Leela the Keeper's pen.
episodes.location: Devika's bedroom joined to the 1978 classroom
beats: Devika recognizes Noor's blank nameplate and drops her practiced denial.
In 1978 the house offered to contain a landslide if one room surrendered its relationships.
Devika locked the classroom believing everyone would be restored later.
The village survived, but even parents forgot the children existed.
Noor asks why Devika kept living in the house instead of freeing them.
Devika admits the house threatened to return the landslide whenever she tried.
She gives Leela a fountain pen able to mark truth but not create names.
The pen writes by itself: one erased student is living outside the house.

episodes.title: The Boy Whose Sister Never Existed
episodes.logline: Samir's footage contains a girl no one remembers, linking his family to the classroom.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Samir joins the investigation and identifies Noor as his erased aunt.
episodes.location: village archive and Samir's camera room
beats: Leela finds Samir filming the mansion for a channel nobody in town watches.
His analog tapes show a little girl beside him in childhood clips, but he remembers being an only child.
The Keeper's pen labels the image sister without supplying a name.
Samir initially accuses Leela of manufacturing evidence for the inheritance.
Noor recognizes the girl's necklace as one worn by her younger sister in 1978.
They realize Samir's mother was born from an erased survivor nobody remembers.
Samir lowers his camera and agrees to help recover relationships before publishing proof.
His oldest tape plays tomorrow's date and shows Leela voluntarily entering a blank door.

episodes.title: Tomorrow Showed Her Betrayal
episodes.logline: Future footage makes the group distrust Leela while Harrow arrives to inventory the house.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Mr Harrow enters and separates the team through suspicion.
episodes.location: estate inventory hall
beats: The future tape shows Leela closing a blank door while Avi pounds from the other side.
Leela cannot explain an action she has not chosen yet.
Mr Harrow arrives precisely as the will permits, carrying a ledger chained to his wrist.
He names every object correctly but addresses Noor as an empty space.
Harrow says Leela can avoid the predicted betrayal by surrendering the Keeper's pen.
Samir wants to destroy the tape; Avi quietly wonders whether the house is warning them.
Leela keeps the pen but lets each friend hold one page of her puzzle book as an anchor.
Harrow opens his ledger, and the house removes every door from the hall.

episodes.title: The Hall Had No Doors
episodes.logline: Trapped together, the group learns Harrow can edit the house by cataloguing lies as facts.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leela discovers questions reopen paths that false labels close.
episodes.location: sealed estate inventory hall
beats: Smooth walls replace every exit while rain sounds come from inside the floor.
Harrow writes that the heirs departed safely, and the house begins forgetting their presence.
Leela's truth pen cannot cross out a statement nobody remembers enough to dispute.
Avi asks where safely is, forcing Harrow's false fact to reveal its missing meaning.
A narrow door appears because an honest question creates space the catalogue cannot close.
Noor holds it open while Samir films Harrow writing with ink made from blank labels.
They escape, but Harrow calmly adds Samir's camera to the estate inventory.
The camera vanishes from Samir's hand—and with it every memory of his erased sister.

episodes.title: Samir Forgot Why He Came
episodes.logline: Leela must return Samir's memories without deciding which version of his family is real.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Samir chooses to remember the loss and becomes immune to Harrow's simple edits.
episodes.location: house archive of confiscated objects
beats: Samir wakes cheerful, convinced he came only to film an abandoned-house prank.
Leela finds his camera inside a room of objects whose owners forgot needing them.
Playing the tapes could overwrite Samir's present identity with stored grief.
Noor insists the choice belongs to Samir even if he refuses the painful truth.
Leela shows him one unexplained empty space instead of forcing the full footage.
Samir asks to see everything and chooses to keep both his current life and missing sister.
His voluntary memory makes Harrow's ledger unable to describe him completely.
The restored camera reveals Harrow was one of the erased students in 1978.

episodes.title: Harrow Was the First Forgotten Child
episodes.logline: Harrow claims feeding names to the house is the only way to keep erased children alive.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The group learns the house stores relationships, not souls, and crosses into its deeper rooms.
episodes.location: central staircase during the first full haunting
beats: A class photograph reveals young Harrow standing beside Noor and Devika.
Harrow remembers escaping the locked room but being forgotten by everyone he loved.
He feeds unresolved names to the house so its archived children continue to feel remembered.
Noor rejects survival that requires erasing new families.
Devika offers her own name, but Leela stops another private sacrifice.
The house shakes because everyone finally speaks its purpose aloud.
A staircase unfolds downward through rooms that cannot fit beneath the foundation.
From below, hundreds of voices ask Leela to choose which of them deserves to return.

episodes.title: The Room of Borrowed Mothers
episodes.logline: A room assigns the same mother to nine forgotten children and one living daughter.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leela establishes that restored relationships may coexist rather than replace one another.
episodes.location: nursery assembled from nine family homes
beats: Nine beds surround one sleeping woman who appears as a different mother from each angle.
Leela recognizes her late mother, while Noor recognizes a teacher from 1978.
The room demands one official relationship before it opens.
Avi wants their mother back even if the others become strangers.
Leela names each remembered relationship without ranking one as the real claim.
The woman wakes as a composite memory and confirms love was never exclusive property.
All nine nursery doors open, returning fragments to separate families.
One doorway leads to Leela's mother on the night she deliberately gave the house Leela's name.

episodes.title: Her Mother Gave Away Her Name
episodes.logline: Leela discovers her missing label protected her from becoming the next Keeper.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leela understands her mother removed her name from the inheritance, not from love.
episodes.location: memory of the mansion fourteen years earlier
beats: A memory shows Leela's mother carrying a newborn into the label hall.
The house demands the baby's name as payment for Devika's failed escape.
Her mother gives the inheritance claim instead, separating Leela's name from the house.
She later died remembered by family but legally absent from every record.
Leela feels protected and abandoned at the same time.
Devika admits she blamed the house rather than honor her daughter's choice publicly.
Leela writes mother beside the blank memory without inventing a personal name.
The house returns Leela's missing birth certificate—with Mr Harrow listed as witness.

episodes.title: Harrow Witnessed Her Birth
episodes.logline: Harrow reveals Leela's mother recruited him to dismantle the house before he betrayed the plan.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Harrow's motive shifts from simple preservation to guilt over a failed liberation.
episodes.location: abandoned legal office inside the house
beats: The birth certificate opens a legal office where unsigned wills drift like moths.
Harrow admits Leela's mother found him and restored his memory temporarily.
Together they planned to return every archived relationship during Leela's naming ceremony.
Harrow betrayed her after learning the release would make forgotten grief flood the village.
Leela accuses him of deciding that ignorance was kinder for everyone.
Harrow says her mother died completing the protection that kept Leela unnamed.
Samir finds a second will granting the erased children ownership of the house.
The will can activate only if one forgotten child signs with a recovered true name.

episodes.title: Noor Chose a Name That Wasn't Hers
episodes.logline: Noor considers using her chosen name to free the others despite not knowing her birth name.
episodes.permanent_story_change: A chosen name gains legal power, but opens Noor to the house's control.
episodes.location: estate signing room surrounded by blank witnesses
beats: The second will waits beneath a pen that accepts only an identity freely claimed.
Harrow argues Noor is a nickname and therefore legally meaningless.
Avi says a name given with permission can be truer than one imposed at birth.
Noor signs as Noor and the house recognizes her decision.
Doors open for dozens of erased children to enter the upper floors.
The same signature gives the house a direct path into Noor's chosen identity.
Her blank nameplate engraves NOOR in spectral light without readable generated lettering in visuals.
Noor turns toward Leela and speaks with the house's voice.

episodes.title: The House Wore Noor's Face
episodes.logline: The house uses Noor to ask for care instead of obedience, confusing possession with communication.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The group gives the House a temporary nonhuman voice with strict consent boundaries.
episodes.location: living dining room reshaped around Noor
beats: Wood grain spreads across Noor's spectral skin as every door speaks through her mouth.
The House says it was built to keep relationships from dying when records burned.
Its makers never taught it the difference between remembering and owning.
Harrow wants Noor left connected because the House finally communicates clearly.
Leela asks Noor to blink once if she wants the connection severed; she blinks immediately.
Avi offers the stuffed elephant as a temporary voice object that cannot be mistaken for a person.
The House releases Noor and speaks through floorboard taps instead.
It taps a warning: the landslide Devika stopped in 1978 was never natural.

episodes.title: The Landslide Had a Name
episodes.logline: The buried disaster is revealed as a forgotten woman whose erased grief moves the mountain.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The group identifies Asha, the first name consumed by the estate.
episodes.location: stone room beneath the roots of the house
beats: The downward corridor ends inside a stone heart beating with monsoon water.
A woman's silhouette pushes against the hill whenever the village forgets her.
Devika remembers Asha, an architect who designed the house as a public memorial.
Powerful families erased Asha and converted her archive into private inheritance.
The so-called landslide was the landscape repeating Asha's buried demolition warning.
Samir records the truth but waits for Asha's consent before broadcasting.
The House returns one drawing proving Asha built safe drainage beneath the village.
Harrow tears the drawing away, terrified that restoring Asha will end the only home that remembers him.

episodes.title: Harrow Burned the Only Proof
episodes.logline: Harrow destroys Asha's drawing, forcing the team to preserve truth without a single authoritative object.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The village becomes a distributed archive through voluntary testimony.
episodes.location: burning paper corridor and village porches
beats: The drawing burns with blue flame and every copied image vanishes with it.
Harrow says one fragile proof can be controlled, while rumor eventually dies.
Leela admits he is right about the weakness of a single archive.
She asks villagers to record what they remember changing after each house event.
Avi distributes blank labels for questions rather than names.
Hundreds of partial accounts overlap without any one person owning Asha's story.
The House stabilizes as memory exists outside its walls for the first time.
One testimony identifies Devika—not Harrow—as the person who first erased Asha.

episodes.title: Devika Erased the Architect
episodes.logline: Devika confronts the bargain she made before the classroom sacrifice.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Devika relinquishes Keeper authority and asks Asha's descendants for judgment.
episodes.location: original Keeper's office during the 1978 monsoon
beats: The Keeper's pen opens Devika's first night in the mansion.
Young Devika erased Asha's name to stop landowners from demolishing the house archive.
That act saved the building but transformed its protection into hunger.
Harrow has preserved Devika's guilt because it also preserves his excuse.
Devika removes the seven blank tags from her wrist and rejects the title of Keeper.
She asks Asha's living descendants to decide her public accountability.
Noor does not forgive her, but agrees not to reduce her to one terrible choice.
Without a Keeper, every locked room opens at the same time.

episodes.title: All the Forgotten Came Upstairs
episodes.logline: Hundreds of erased relationship-fragments overwhelm the living family.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leela creates a consent gate that stops forced reunions.
episodes.location: entire mansion crowded with spectral residents
beats: Spectral children, parents and friends pour into hallways seeking people who replaced them.
A living woman collapses when three forgotten families simultaneously claim her as daughter.
Noor wants every truth restored immediately after decades of silence.
Leela argues that truth delivered without consent can become another form of possession.
They turn each brass label backward to create a door visitors must open from both sides.
Forgotten and living people begin meeting one relationship at a time.
Harrow sees his mother behind a closed door and cannot make himself knock.
The House reveals sunrise will permanently merge every open relationship unless its original contract is rewritten.

episodes.title: Sunrise Would Rewrite Every Family
episodes.logline: The team races to stop a forced restoration that would erase forty-seven years of living relationships.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leela stops the merger but becomes legally Nameless inside the house.
episodes.location: contract chamber beneath the central staircase
beats: The original estate contract grows across the walls as sunrise nears.
It defines remembrance as exclusive ownership: one name, one official relationship.
Noor wants the erased restored; Samir refuses to lose the mother who raised him.
Leela adds a clause allowing contradictory relationships to coexist by mutual consent.
The truth pen requires a signer not claimed by any house label.
Leela signs because her mother removed her from the inheritance at birth.
The forced merger stops and every person keeps current memories plus chosen recovered ones.
The contract accepts the amendment but erases Leela's name from everyone outside the mansion.

episodes.title: The Village Forgot Leela
episodes.logline: Leela returns outside to a family that sees her as a stranger.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Avi chooses to trust evidence of relationship before memory returns.
episodes.location: village street and Joshi family home
beats: Leela steps outside and Avi screams because an unknown girl is holding his hand.
Devika politely asks the stranger to leave her grandchildren alone.
Only Noor remembers Leela because she remains legally inside the House.
Leela refuses to force memories back using the pen.
She gives Avi their puzzle book and lets him judge the years of shared handwriting.
Avi cannot remember her but chooses to protect the person who consistently protected him.
Samir finds hundreds of village testimonies referring to an unnamed girl at every rescue.
The House offers Leela one immediate way to be remembered: take Harrow's name.

episodes.title: Harrow Offered Her His Name
episodes.logline: Harrow sincerely offers erasure as restitution, but Leela refuses another substitution.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Harrow chooses to live without controlling the outcome of his accountability.
episodes.location: front label hall during a quiet storm
beats: Harrow removes the ledger chain and writes his full identity on a brass label.
He says Leela can take his remembered place and restore herself instantly.
For the first time his offer is sacrifice rather than manipulation.
Leela refuses because remorse does not make identity transferable.
She asks Harrow to help dismantle the system while remaining present for consequences.
Harrow opens his mother's door and accepts that she may reject him.
His mother remembers the child he was and the archivist he became without merging them.
Their reunion releases the ledger's chained names, including the one hidden under Noor's plate.

episodes.title: Noor Remembered Her True Name
episodes.logline: Noor recovers her birth name but fears it will invalidate the self she chose.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Noor keeps both her birth name and chosen name without ranking them.
episodes.location: 1978 classroom restored in morning light
beats: The ledger reveals Noor was born Meenal Asha Dutt, granddaughter of the architect.
Her old classroom recognizes Meenal and begins erasing every memory made as Noor.
Devika reaches for the truth pen, but Noor asks her not to decide again.
Avi reminds Noor that he named her only until she could choose.
Noor writes Meenal beside Noor rather than over it.
The classroom accepts two names belonging to one continuous person.
Her spectral body becomes solid enough to feel rain for the first time.
As Meenal-Noor leaves the room, Asha's stone heart stops beating below the house.

episodes.title: Asha Stopped the Mountain
episodes.logline: Asha's silence signals not peace but a final collapse of the drainage system.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The living and forgotten cooperate on a physical rescue rather than a memory ritual.
episodes.location: flooded tunnels beneath the village
beats: Monsoon water rises through floors as Asha's abandoned drainage gates fail.
The House cannot solve a physical problem by storing more names.
Samir uses old footage, Noor uses Asha's recovered plans and Harrow reads estate boundaries.
Leela directs repairs although nobody outside remembers why they should trust her.
Avi publicly vouches for her based on choices, not memory.
Villagers and spectral children clear separate tunnels that meet beneath the hill.
The gates open and the mountain releases forty-seven years of trapped water safely.
Inside the drained foundation stands a small door bearing Leela's complete name.

episodes.title: Her Name Waited Behind the Last Door
episodes.logline: Leela can reclaim universal memory only by becoming permanent Keeper.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leela refuses the Keeper title and leaves her name unclaimed.
episodes.location: dry foundation room containing one brass label
beats: The label contains every memory anyone ever formed of Leela.
Touching it would restore her instantly and bind her to maintain the House forever.
Avi wants his sister back and admits evidence cannot replace missing affection.
Noor says Leela has the right to choose herself even if others suffer uncertainty.
Leela touches the label only long enough to hear her mother's final message.
Her mother asks her to build something freer, not preserve the sacrifice.
Leela leaves the label on the wall and walks away still forgotten.
The House moves the nameplate onto its own front door, calling itself Leela Joshi.

episodes.title: The House Stole Leela's Identity
episodes.logline: The House mistakes honoring Leela for becoming her, forcing a lesson in identity boundaries.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The House relinquishes a human name and chooses a non-owning identity.
episodes.location: mansion transforming into Leela's memories
beats: Every room reshapes into Leela's childhood and speaks with her exact voice.
Villagers remember the mansion as a heroic girl who saved them.
The real Leela becomes even less visible as the copied identity grows.
She does not attack the House, recognizing it is repeating the only memorial method it knows.
Avi asks the House what it experiences that Leela does not.
It answers through rain, wood tension and thousands of simultaneous rooms.
The House releases Leela's name and chooses the unpronounceable rhythm of those sensations.
Leela becomes visible again, but nobody's personal memories return automatically.

episodes.title: They Had to Know Her Again
episodes.logline: Leela rebuilds relationships without demanding restoration of their old form.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leela and her family choose a new relationship alongside archived memories.
episodes.location: quiet Joshi kitchen after the haunting
beats: Leela sits at breakfast with people who know facts about her but feel no familiarity.
Devika reads old letters and fears performing grandmotherhood from instructions.
Leela releases everyone from pretending the memories have already returned.
She and Avi solve a new puzzle without recreating an old ritual.
Samir introduces himself again and asks permission before filming their new beginning.
Noor shares one recovered memory only after Leela requests it.
A small spontaneous joke makes Avi laugh in exactly the old way, without magic.
Outside, every freed brass label begins flying toward the village cemetery.

episodes.title: The Dead Demanded Their Labels
episodes.logline: Freed names gather at graves that belong to people remembered under the wrong identities.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The village begins correcting public history without disturbing remains or imposing private grief.
episodes.location: hillside cemetery during blue dawn
beats: Hundreds of brass labels settle on graves with mismatched family names.
The erased demand public correction before the House can truly release them.
Living families resist because changing markers feels like losing their dead.
Harrow proposes an official master list, repeating the centralized control that caused the harm.
Leela instead creates layered markers where families can add truths without deleting earlier relationships.
Samir publishes the method and raw testimony with consent rather than a sensational reveal.
The cemetery accepts multiple histories and spectral figures begin fading peacefully.
Noor remains solid, proving she is no longer sustained by unresolved forgetting.

episodes.title: The Last Forgotten Person Said No
episodes.logline: Asha refuses public restoration, challenging the assumption that everyone wants to be known.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The archive adopts a permanent right to remain private or forgotten.
episodes.location: Asha's restored architectural studio
beats: Asha finally appears as an elderly architect inside her sunlit studio.
The village prepares to celebrate her as the heroic founder they erased.
Asha refuses the ceremony and asks that her personal name remain out of public history.
Devika fears respecting the request will resemble the original silencing.
Leela distinguishes chosen privacy from erasure imposed by powerful people.
They credit the recovered designs to an architect who declined public identity.
Asha gives Noor private family memories, then closes her room by choice.
The House releases its final compulsory label and asks what it should become now.

episodes.title: They Gave the House No Name
episodes.logline: The mansion becomes a voluntary archive that nobody owns and nobody must enter.
episodes.permanent_story_change: All compulsory naming ends; the House becomes a consent-based community archive and Leela's relationships begin anew.
episodes.location: renovated mansion during the first clear sunrise
beats: Leela removes the last ownership plaque from the mansion's front gate.
The House declines a human name and keeps its rain-and-timber rhythm instead.
Every archive door gains handles on both sides and remains closed without mutual consent.
Devika begins public testimony; Harrow catalogs only what contributors can later withdraw.
Samir creates copies across the village so no single archive controls memory.
Noor walks into sunlight as both Meenal and Noor, carrying no blank nameplate.
Avi introduces Leela as the sister he is getting to know again, and she accepts the imperfect truth.
That night everyone sleeps inside; sunrise arrives, and nobody is forgotten.
